title: test(app-shell): deepen the three placeholder-branch DOM-leak fixtures
body:
Fixes #5630

## What changed

`element:definition-list`, `element:repeater` and `element:metadata_viewer` were swept by `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx` only through their empty-state placeholder branch — the element each renderer spreads onto once it has real content was never reached, so their clean reading covered a branch that never spreads. This PR deepens all three fixtures past the placeholder, per triage's shape:

- **`element:definition-list`** — authors `items` (pure schema, no host needed).
- **`element:repeater`** — adds a per-target `AdapterCtx.Provider` fixture (`REPEATER_FAKE_ADAPTER`) whose `find()` returns a row.
- **`element:metadata_viewer`** — adds a per-target `MetadataCtx.Provider` fixture (`METADATA_HOST_CONTEXT`) resolving a `permission` metadata item.

`FAKE_ADAPTER`'s empty answer stays exactly as load-bearing for the other 155 targets as before — both new hosts are additive and scoped to the one target that declares them.

## A premise correction, measured rather than assumed

The issue describes `element:repeater`'s mechanism as "the sweep's `FAKE_ADAPTER` answers with no rows by design." That undersold it. `RepeaterRenderer` reads data through `useAdapter()` → `AdapterCtx` — a **separate** context from `SchemaRendererProvider`'s `dataSource` prop, which `FAKE_ADAPTER` populates. `AdapterCtx` is never wired anywhere in this sweep, so `useAdapter()` always returned `null`, and the renderer's effect short-circuits on `!adapter` **before ever calling `.find()`** — on any fixture. Widening what `FAKE_ADAPTER` returns would have changed nothing; the fix needed a new, additive `AdapterCtx.Provider` host instead. (Traced in source, then confirmed the hard way: an early attempt at authoring `items`/`object` directly on the schema top level did nothing either, for an unrelated reason below.)

## All three renderers read CLEAN — traced, not just measured

Neither `basic/data-list.tsx` nor `basic/metadata-viewer.tsx` spreads `{...props}` (or any rest of the props `SchemaRenderer` hands these components) onto a DOM element anywhere in either file, in any branch — every host element is hand-built from named fields only. So the canary families this sweep plants have no path to the DOM in any branch of these three renderers, regardless of fixture depth.

**Reverse-verified per target**, not just traced: a deliberate leak (`zzinjectedleak="…"`) was planted on each now-reachable populated-branch host element (`<dl>`, `<ul>`, the `Shell` wrapper `<div>`), confirmed present on disk (`grep -c`), and the sweep run again:

```
FAIL … element:definition-list
+ element:definition-list leaked 1 non-DOM attribute(s):
+   <dl> leaked zzinjectedleak="objectui-5630-instrument-check"

FAIL … element:repeater
+ element:repeater leaked 1 non-DOM attribute(s):
+   <ul> leaked zzinjectedleak="objectui-5630-instrument-check"

FAIL … element:metadata_viewer
+ element:metadata_viewer leaked 1 non-DOM attribute(s):
+   <div> leaked zzinjectedleak="objectui-5630-instrument-check"

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  3 failed | 197 passed (200)
```

Exactly the three deepened targets failed, nothing else regressed — proving the instrument catches a real leak on the branch this PR newly reaches, which the old placeholder-only fixture structurally could not (the injected line lives after the early-return the empty-state branch takes). The mutation was never committed — reverted via `git checkout -- <path>` (both files were otherwise clean) before the real fix was built on top.

## `READY_OVERRIDE_REASONS`: shrinks by two, not three

Triage's dispatch predicted the list would shrink by exactly three (and flagged it explicitly as a prediction to verify, not assume). Measured: it shrinks from **six entries to four**.

- `element:definition-list` and `element:repeater` drop their entries **entirely** — their populated `<dl>`/`<ul>` both fold `schema?.className` into their own `cn(...)`, so once there's real content the shared readiness class reaches the DOM the same as any plain target, and the default `COMPONENTS_READY` selector matches.
- `element:metadata_viewer` does **not** drop out. `ElementMetadataViewerRenderer`'s `Shell` wrapper hardcodes its className in every branch — `ViewerProps` declares no `className` field at all — so no amount of fixture depth changes that; it's a fact about the renderer, out of this test-fixtures-only card's scope. Its entry is **rewritten**, not deleted, to name the real populated render instead of the not-found placeholder.

## Testing

Repo convention: `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` from repo root (never `pnpm --filter`, per `scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs`).

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  200 passed (200)
```

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` — clean (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`), after building the package's full dependency closure (`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=4 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`, 29 packages, all succeeded) since `tsconfig.test.json` deliberately resolves `@object-ui/*` through built `.d.ts`.
- `pnpm exec eslint packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx --no-inline-config` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` / `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — clean (empty-frontmatter changeset added; test-only, no release).

All at `94d9cb4df` (this PR's current head).

## Scope

Test fixtures only — no renderer source touched (`basic/data-list.tsx`, `basic/metadata-viewer.tsx` are byte-identical to `main`), no `LEAK_LEDGER` rows added (none of the three leak in the populated branch either).
